reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis incorrectly links low SFE to enhanced cross-slip and reduced work hardening; low SFE typically suppresses cross-slip, promotes planar slip and twinning, and increases work hardening, contradicting established deformation physics.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is detailed and would be decisive, but it is built on a physically flawed premise, so the test as designed would not properly evaluate the intended mechanism.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it is based on a fundamental misunderstanding of stacking fault energy effects on deformation, leading researchers in the wrong direction.
